**SGInnovate**, a government-backed investor and ecosystem builder in Singapore, is inviting advanced students in the **42 Network** to apply for their Summation Programme. SGInnovate supports early-stage deep tech startups in areas like AI, quantum computing, and biotech, playing a key role in Singapore’s innovation ecosystem.

**Prerequisites**:

Only accessible after the completion of the Common Core

**Internship Details**:

Duration: 3–6 months

Brochure: [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1CK8WQfsqHRDLrXmDA-HyOmhtp0NohrXM/view?usp=sharing)

Fully covered: transportation, living expenses, and accommodation in Singapore

**Next Steps**:

Information Session for all advanced students:

📅 March 3rd, 2026

🕤 **9:30–10:30 CET**

**[Join online](https://www.youtube.com/live/YV70xJmdtXg)**

If you have any questions, please submit the [following form](https://tally.42.fr/sg-innovate-event-questions)

Don’t miss this chance to gain invaluable experience in deep tech with a leading Singapore-based innovator!

event.name: Behind the Flags, How the CTF Was Designed - Cyber Saiyan
event.description:
📍 **The Archives**
📅 **20 febbraio 2026**  
🕡 **Ore 18:30 CET**  
📌 **@42 Roma Luiss – Via Marsala 29H (Zona Termini)**  
🌍 **Lingua: Inglese 🇬🇧**

---

**🇮🇹 Descrizione (Italiano)**

**The Road to RomHack Camp 2026 starts here!**

Per la sessione inaugurale di **RomHack Bẏtes**, il team **Cyber Saiyan** insieme a **Fibonhack** – mastermind dietro il RomHack Camp CTF – ci porteranno dietro le quinte di una delle sfide più intense dell’anno.

Racconteranno come è nato, sviluppato e portato a termine il progetto **“From Dusk Till Dawn”**, mostrando cosa significa davvero progettare, costruire e far girare una competizione CTF su larga scala.

**Quali sono le vere sfide nel gestire una CTF ad alto livello?**

Non parliamo solo di flag, ma di:

- 🏗️ Architettura dell’infrastruttura  
- ⚙️ Problemi tecnici e imprevisti  
- 👥 Coordinamento del team  
- 🌙 Gestione della pressione quando la notte si fa lunga  
- 📚 Lezioni imparate sul campo  

Un’occasione unica per scoprire cosa succede davvero dietro le quinte di una competizione internazionale.

---

**🇬🇧 Description (English)**

**The Road to RomHack Camp 2026 starts here!**

For the inaugural **RomHack Bẏtes** session, **Cyber Saiyan** together with **Fibonhack** — the masterminds behind the RomHack Camp CTF — will take us behind the scenes of one of the most intense cybersecurity challenges of the year.

They will share how the **“From Dusk Till Dawn”** project was conceived, designed, and executed, offering a deep dive into what it truly means to build and operate a large-scale CTF competition.

** What are the real challenges of running a high-level CTF?**

Beyond flags and scoring systems, we will explore:

- 🏗️ Infrastructure architecture  
- ⚙️ Technical issues and unexpected failures  
- 👥 Team coordination and operational pressure  
- 🌙 Lessons learned when deadlines are tight and the night gets long  

A unique opportunity to understand what really happens behind the curtain of an international CTF event.

---

**About RomHack Bẏtes**

**Bẏtes** is RomHack’s new technical meetup series — a space for the community to gather, share research, and fuel the journey toward RomHack Camp at Flaminio Village this September.

⚠️ **Attendance at 42 Roma Luiss is limited.** If you can no longer attend, please let us know so we can free up your spot for someone else.

🔗 More info: **https://romhack.io/bytes**

- Always remain polite, courteous, respectful, and constructive.
  The well-being of the community depends on it.

- Work with the evaluated person (or group) to identify any potential
  issues in their work.
  Take the time to discuss and debate the problems you’ve found.

- Keep in mind that your peers may have interpreted the project’s
  instructions and scope differently.
  Stay open-minded and grade them as honestly as possible.

- The educational value of this process relies entirely on serious and
  fair peer evaluations.
scale.guidelines_md:
- Only grade the work that is in the student's or group's Git repository.

- Double-check that the Git repository belongs to the student or group.
  Ensure the work is for the relevant project and verify that "git clone"
  is used in an empty folder.

- Carefully check that no malicious aliases have been used to mislead
  you into evaluating something other than the official repository's
  content.

- To avoid surprises, both the evaluating and evaluated students must 
  review any scripts used to facilitate grading.

- If the evaluating student has not yet completed the project, they
  must read the entire subject before starting the defense.

- Use the flags available on the scale to signal issues such as an
  empty repository, a non-functioning program, norm errors, or cheating.
  In these cases, the grading ends immediately, and the final grade
  is 0 (-42 in case of cheating).

 - However, except for cases of cheating, you are encouraged to discuss
  the work, even if incomplete, to help identify issues and avoid
  repeating mistakes.

- During the defense, no segmentation faults (segfaults), unexpected
  crashes, or uncontrolled terminations are allowed.
  If any occur, the final grade is 0, and you must use the appropriate flag.

- You should never edit any file except for a configuration file (if it exists).
  If editing a file is necessary, discuss the reasons with the evaluated
  student and ensure both agree before proceeding.

- Verify that only the requested files are present in the Git repository.
  If additional files are found, the evaluation stops immediately.

Please adhere to the following rules during the evaluation process:

 - Always remain polite, courteous, respectful, and constructive.
  The well-being of the community depends on it.

 - Work with the evaluated person (or group) to identify any potential
  issues in their work.
  Take the time to discuss and debate the problems you’ve found.

 - Keep in mind that your peers may have interpreted the project’s
  instructions and scope differently.
  Stay open-minded and grade them as honestly as possible.

 - The educational value of this process relies entirely on serious and
  fair peer evaluations.
scale.guidelines_md:
- Only grade the work that is in the student's or group's Git repository.

- Double-check that the Git repository belongs to the student or group.
  Ensure the work is for the relevant project and verify that "git clone"
  is used in an empty folder.

- Carefully check that no malicious aliases have been used to mislead
  you into evaluating something other than the official repository's
  content.

- To avoid surprises, both the evaluating and evaluated students must 
  review any scripts used to facilitate grading.

- If the evaluating student has not yet completed the project, they
  must read the entire subject before starting the defense.

- Use the flags available on the scale to signal issues such as an
  empty repository, a non-functioning program, norm errors, or cheating.
  In these cases, the grading ends immediately, and the final grade
  is 0 (-42 in case of cheating).

- However, except for cases of cheating, you are encouraged to discuss
  the work, even if incomplete, to help identify issues and avoid
  repeating mistakes.

- During the defense, no segmentation faults (segfaults), unexpected
  crashes, or uncontrolled terminations are allowed.
  If any occur, the final grade is 0, and you must use the appropriate flag.

- You should never edit any file except for a configuration file (if it exists).
  If editing a file is necessary, discuss the reasons with the evaluated
  student and ensure both agree before proceeding.

- Verify that only the requested files are present in the Git repository.
  If additional files are found, the evaluation stops immediately.
